source.topic: what hydrogen peroxide actually does around the house (real, sourced) vs. the folklore piled on top of it, especially the outdated advice to pour it on cuts
source.angle: the honest version of the niche's current hottest format ('X hydrogen peroxide hacks', 'X don't want you to know about hydrogen peroxide'). Walt tells the real, defensible version: it IS a genuine EPA-recognized disinfectant when used at the right concentration with real dwell/contact time (most people wipe it off too soon), but modern clinical guidance has REVERSED on the most common home use - pouring it on cuts, which is now understood to damage healing tissue. Same honest-differentiator strategy that worked on video 3 (mosquito-trap-truth).
source.research_note: tools/yt_research.py --niche home-hacks targeted query: 'hydrogen peroxide' format is CURRENTLY the dominant live pattern, ahead of the mosquito/pest format used for video 3. 'Stop Wasting Stuff' - 9 Things Exterminators Don't Want You to Know About Hydrogen Peroxide - 29,968 v/d, 2.4M views/81d, live and recurring across 24h/30d/365d windows, multiple independent channels cloning the '[profession] doesn't want you to know' framing successfully. tools/validate_topic.py hit YouTube API quota exhaustion (429 Too Many Requests) on both attempts before a clean read could be obtained - first attempt's winnability section (unaffected by the search-call 429) showed up to 113.6x breakout on a 1,870-sub channel using this exact framing. User explicitly chose to proceed on this partial-but-strong evidence rather than wait for quota reset, given time already invested and the strength/consistency of the yt_research signal. Full evidence in conversation transcript 2026-08-04.
source.honesty_note: Deliberately NOT using the literal '[profession] doesn't want you to know' framing in the title/thumbnail - that's an unfalsifiable claim about people's motives that doesn't fit Walt's voice or honesty_guard. Built the same differentiator through Walt's own honest myth-vs-reality framing instead.

honesty_guard: see niches/home-hacks.json script.honesty_guard - every number defensible. Central claims sourced to: Wayne State University Office of Environmental Health & Safety (EPA-registered disinfectant concentration/contact-time guidance - note: source page is about lab/research-facility surface disinfection, not literally household use, so narration must frame this as the general EPA-registered-disinfectant principle, not claim the source specifically endorses kitchen-counter use at that exact concentration) and Healogics wound care clinical guidance (modern clinical consensus against hydrogen peroxide on wounds - corroborated by multiple independent medical sources found via WebSearch: Mayo-adjacent, University of Utah Health, WCEI, though the single fetched source itself doesn't name CDC/WHO directly, so narration should say 'wound care experts/current guidelines' rather than attribute to a specific named body it doesn't cite). Never claim a specific profession 'doesn't want you to know' anything - that's exactly the overclaim this video avoids repeating from the viral clones.
